1

Purpose

This procedure enables users to quickly create a new dashboard and share it with their team by generating a shareable link. This allows for easy distribution of key task status information, fostering collaboration and improved team visibility. Following these steps ensures consistent dashboard creation and sharing across the organization.

The process covers the following tasks:

  • Create a New dashboard
  • Add a Bar Chart Widget
  • Edit Widget Title and Share
  • Copy the Shareable Link
In short

The session demonstrated how to create and share a dashboard. The user began by navigating to the dashboards menu and selecting "New dashboard," naming it "Weekly Overview" and choosing a blank template. A bar chart widget was then added, configured to display tasks by status. The widget's title was edited to read "tasks this week" for clarity. Finally, the user enabled sharing via a link and copied that link for distribution, completing the demonstration of how to share the dashboard with a team.

Before you start

Have the following ready before you begin.

What you need
Access to Grafana
Permission to create dashboards in Grafana
A pre-existing data source connected to Grafana
Ability to edit widget titles and sharing options in Grafana
Internet access to copy the shareable link

Part C

Edit Widget Title and Share

00:39

C2

Questions and answers

Questions raised in the recording, plus ones a new reader may have.

Why is it recommended to use a blank template when creating a new dashboard?+

According to the provided instructions, it is recommended to use a blank template when creating a new dashboard because it allows you to start fresh and customize the dashboard to your specific needs. After selecting the blank template, you can then add widgets to populate the dashboard.

What does "anyone with the link" mean when sharing a dashboard?+

When sharing a dashboard, "anyone with the link" means that the dashboard will be accessible to anyone who possesses the copied link. This setting allows for broad distribution, as it doesn't require specific user permissions or logins to view the dashboard. Once the link is copied, it can be shared via email, messaging, or any other method.

When should I consider using a different widget type instead of a bar chart?+

The transcript does not provide information about when to use a different widget type; it only describes how to add and edit a bar chart widget. To create the bar chart, first select it, then add a widget to an empty dashboard, and finally edit the chart by typing "tasks this week" and saving. The chart will then be ready for use.

What specific data source is used when selecting "tasks by status" for the widget?+

The data source used when selecting "tasks by status" is simply referred to as "tasks by status" itself, as indicated by the instruction to "choose tasks by status." This selection is made when adding a widget to an initially empty dashboard.

What's the difference between sharing a dashboard with specific team members versus using the "anyone with the link" option?+

Sharing a dashboard with specific team members requires individually granting access, while the "anyone with the link" option makes the dashboard accessible to anyone who possesses the copied link. The latter option is enabled by switching on the "anyone with the link" setting when sharing. This allows for broader distribution of the dashboard.

If I want to track something other than tasks, can I use a different data source when adding a widget?+

Yes, you can track something other than tasks; the process involves selecting a data source when adding a widget. To do this, you would first choose tasks by status, then click "add" to begin the process. After that, you can click "Add widget" and then "edit" to specify the data you want to display.
